SMTO-FIL-0012 — SMTO couldn't open the folder it works from on that computer

GUID: 1789df83-6b74-4e0b-9a8c-b1f6d5f04989
Slug: file-invalid-working-directory
Domain: FIL · Subsystem: files

What happened

  • SMTO starts each file action from a working folder on the Gateway's computer (the Gateway is the helper program SMTO uses there). That folder is missing or couldn't be opened, so nothing was run or changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. On the computer that runs the Gateway, check that the folder shown in Technical details still exists and hasn't been renamed, moved or deleted. SMTO stops when the folder it should start in is no longer there.
  2. Open Settings › Setup › Gateways, select Edit for this Gateway, and check Terminal working directory. Set it to a folder that exists, or leave it blank. This setting decides which folder SMTO starts in; blank uses the Gateway's own work folder.
  3. If the folder is on a USB drive or network share, reconnect that drive, then ask SMTO in the conversation to try the step again. A disconnected drive makes the folder unreachable even when the setting is right.

What success looks like

  • The file step runs and SMTO shows the folder's contents or finishes the action.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages this Gateway. For a saved Run or schedule, don't quietly point it at a different computer or folder just to get past this; that changes where its work happens.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Gateway could not resolve the file operation's working directory or enabled guard root because the path does not exist, is not a directory, or could not be resolved on the target filesystem.

What this means

  • Gateway working-directory resolution raised InvalidWorkingDirectory for the requested execution directory or enabled guard root. File and transfer receipts retain per-item execution, publication, cleanup and partial-effect facts. These explanations do not modify files, weaken path guards or replay a write; reconcile the original state before further mutation.

Why this can happen

  • Gateway working-directory resolution raised InvalidWorkingDirectory for the requested execution directory or enabled guard root.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare requested_cwd and resolved cwd on the selected Gateway, including existence, directory type and accepted scope.

How to fix it

  • Compare the cwd and requested_cwd facts in the receipt with the Gateway host. Restore that directory, or correct the Gateway's Terminal working directory (Settings › Setup › Gateways) or GATEWAY_WORKDIR so it resolves to an existing directory (gateway_core/file_paths.FilePaths.cwd, file_provider.FileProvider.execute).
  • Select an existing directory within the authorized workspace on the selected target.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended existing directory resolves through the ordinary Gateway working-directory boundary.

What not to do

  • Do not silently substitute a different target for a saved run or move its existing execution authority.

Technical notes

  • File and transfer receipts retain per-item execution, publication, cleanup and partial-effect facts. These explanations do not modify files, weaken path guards or replay a write; reconcile the original state before further mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
